title: Pierced for Our Transgressions
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: "Who has believed what he has heard from us?" Read Isaiah 53 slowly, and let the specificity of God's plan cast aside your doubts.
exhortation: This morning I just want to take some time to meditate on Isaiah 53. A couple of comments, and then we'll read it and think on it.

Verse 1 asks, "Who has believed what he has heard from us? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?" Think about that question. Are your eyes shut this morning? The eyes of the people of Israel were blinded. They couldn't see what was so plain. Even when Jesus was physically with them on the road to Emmaus, he had to spell it out: "O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken! Was it not necessary that the Christ should suffer these things and enter into his glory?" And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.

We need to be given eyes to see that Jesus is the Messiah, the one Isaiah prophesied about. As you read this chapter, let the power of God's plan astound you. Let the specificity of the prophecies leave you in awe, and let the impossibility of it being chance cast aside your doubts.
Lord, bless your word as we read. May it bear fruit and multiply a harvest of faith. Open our eyes to see you, and give us eyes of faith.
prayer: Lord, thank you for your plan. From all eternity you planned to come, to show us grace, love and kindness and rescue us from our sin. Thank you, Jesus, our Shepherd, for going after the sheep and laying down your life for us foolish, wandering sheep. We are so grateful.
May our worship be a sweet aroma to you. Fill our hearts with gratitude today for who you are and what you've done. Let this truth affect our hearts and our actions today. In Jesus' name.
